# ADDENDUM 15 — July 15, 2026: Deck v3 — Teddy's Revisions (Env-Perception Pillar, Merged Team Slide, Bio Update, Subscription Reframe)

## 141. TEDDY'S DECK FEEDBACK — four changes requested (relayed via Josh; Josh approved "make all the changes you'd recommend")

Teddy reviewed the v2 deck and requested: (1) the fourth software pillar should highlight **environment perception with real-time and static obstacle avoidance for motion-path optimization** — he considers it more powerful than the 3D/TCP viewer UI; (2) the Slide 10 "Why Us" felt redundant with Slide 13 (Team) and could be replaced/merged; (3) his own bio blurb should change from "leads machining & assembly" to reflect **product & software development engineering**; (4) a strategic concern on the **mandatory subscription** — every other cobot supplier (UR, Standard Bots' planned AI-native software) bundles software free, so customers may resist a hard subscription.

## 142. DECK v3 — the four changes as executed (16 slides, down from 17)

**(a) Pillar 04 swap (formerly slide 5).** "3D + TCP Control" replaced by:
> **04 Environment Perception** — "Cameras + LiDAR see static and moving obstacles in real time — the robot optimizes its motion paths around them, automatically."
The 3D/TCP viewer is no longer a headline pillar; it survives implicitly (demo, product screenshots). Slide 4's AI-brain box subtitle updated to "...Part recognition · Environment perception" and the Roadmap PILOT card now reads "Environment-perception viewer complete" (was "3D/TCP viewer complete").

**(b) Slides 10 + 13 merged → one slide at position 10; deck is now 16 pages.** Structure: eyebrow "WHY US · THE TEAM", headline "Operators, not theorists.", sub-line "The customer, the operator, and the AI layer are all co-founders — a closed loop competitors can't copy." Three cards each carry BOTH the closed-loop role eyebrow AND the full bio: THE CUSTOMER / Patrick Smith / Co-Founder · Supply Chain (full v2 slide-13 bio + captive-test-bed line); THE OPERATOR / Teddy Simpson / Co-Founder · Engineering (new bio, below); THE AI LAYER / Josh Edhlund / Co-Founder · Business & Capital (v2 slide-13 bio + "Leads the AI platform and the raise"). Footer italic line preserves the v2 slide-10 supporting claims (Wisconsin manufacturing at 60–70% margins; floor-validated features; brain improves across segments). NOTE: this also resolves the open §73 item "rename THE AI LAYER eyebrow" — the eyebrow is retained inside the merged slide as Josh's card header.

**(c) Teddy's bio — approved compromise wording.** Teddy asked for "leads product & software development engineering"; flagged that verbatim it collides with Josh's AI-platform positioning and the closed-loop narrative. Josh approved the recommended blend:
> "Mechanical engineer. Ex-Tesla Powerwall & battery pack line design. MS Product Development, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. Leads product engineering — from machining and assembly in our Boyceville shop to hardware-software integration on the platform."
Eyebrow stays "Co-Founder · Engineering" / "THE OPERATOR".

**(d) Subscription reframe — "core software included, the AI brain is the subscription."** Rationale: competitors bundle software free, but none bundle a continuously learning brain; charge for the intelligence, not the software. Changes: Slide 6 (Business Model) banner now reads "CORE SOFTWARE INCLUDED — THE AI BRAIN IS THE SUBSCRIPTION · $500–800 / MO PER ROBOT" with sub-line "Competitors bundle software free. Nobody bundles a brain that keeps learning — retraining, retasking, and fleet updates are the paid layer."; Segment 2 card price line now "License + AI subscription". Slide 11 (Unit Economics) column header "SUBSCRIPTION" → "AI SUBSCRIPTION"; Comparable row → "Others bundle software — none bundle a learning brain". Slide 12 assumption bullet → "Every unit carries the AI subscription (~$7K/yr avg)". Pricing numbers unchanged ($500–800/mo, ~$7K/yr avg), so the financial model is untouched. Alternates discussed but not adopted: first-year-included converting at renewal; usage/outcome pricing per retask. Open for founder discussion if the market pushes back.

## PROCESS LESSONS (88–89)
88. **Co-founder feedback relayed through the account holder still gets a recommendation pass.** Teddy's requested bio wording collided with Josh's locked positioning; presenting a blended alternative and getting Josh's blanket approval ("make all the changes you'd recommend") resolved it in one turn without a rebuild cycle.
89. **Strategic objections (like subscription resistance) are best answered inside the existing model, not by deleting the model.** Reframing "mandatory subscription" as "core software included, the intelligence is subscribed" addressed the competitive-bundling concern while keeping the recurring-revenue layer and all pricing numbers intact.

## 145. PLATFORM SCREENSHOTS SLIDE — deck v4 (17 slides), from Teddy's demo videos

Teddy delivered four screen-capture videos via WeTransfer (July 14): "Robot Perception Creates Keep Out Zones" (104s), "How the 3D Viewer Enables Safe Autonomy" (71s), "How Robot Vision Builds 3D Workspace Understanding" (46s), "Neurobot Part Recognition and 3D Positioning" (68s). All show the live NeuRobots controller UI (RoboAi build, 192.168.1.246).

Frames were extracted with ffmpeg, gradient screen-recording borders auto-cropped (HSV saturation threshold), and each frame hand-cropped to its informative region at a uniform 3.15:1 aspect. Four shots selected:
1. **3D View — static keep-out zones ON, "CLEAR · 7 IN-REACH, NEAREST 277 MM" badge, digital twin + orange obstacle meshes** (from "How the 3D Viewer Enables Safe Autonomy", ~45s) — the environment-perception hero.
2. **Setup & Commissioning Wizard — "Environment baseline scan" step with live LiDAR point cloud** (from "Keep Out Zones", ~40s).
3. **Part Recognition — taught-part library, pickable-face + approach-direction panel** (from "Part Recognition and 3D Positioning", ~45s).
4. **Cameras & LiDAR — dual camera feeds over the live point cloud** (from "3D Workspace Understanding", ~12s).

**New slide inserted at position 6** (after Four Pillars): eyebrow "THE PLATFORM", headline **"Not a concept. Running software."**, 2×2 grid of the four shots with one-line captions tying each to a pillar. Deck is now **17 slides** (footers renumbered); all v3 content otherwise unchanged. Deliverables: **NeuRobots_Investor_Pitch_Deck_v4.pdf** + **deck_v4.html** (screenshots embedded as base64 JPEG, so the HTML is self-contained). This substantially satisfies the long-standing "priority screenshots" pending item (3D viewer, part-recognition overlay, commissioning wizard captured; robot-arm-in-motion photo and program-by-demonstration UI shot still welcome as upgrades).

## PROCESS LESSON (90)
90. **Crop screenshots to the proof point, not the center.** A naive object-fit center-crop of UI frames cut off the exact elements that carry the message (the CLEAR/proximity badge, the wizard heading); pre-cropping each frame to its informative region at a fixed aspect before embedding preserved the evidence the slide exists to show.
